2608.16889.title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory
2608.16889.paper_summary: Long-horizon robot manipulation chains many contact-rich skills into one multi-stage task. Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly master the individual skills, yet the chain still fails: errors compound beyond the policy's ability to correct, and one subtask silently constrains the next. A promising recipe freezes the VLA and puts an LLM agent in charge: it plans in language, moves in free space with analytic primitives, invokes the VLA only for contact-rich segments, and writes adaptation into language memory. Applied to long horizons, it breaks twice. (1) Competence comes from whole-task exploration at test time, whose cost is multiplicative in stages: if one stage needs T episodes, a K-stage task needs about T^K, and a failure does not reveal which stage caused it. (2) It has no representation of transitions: the VLA primitive carries an exit but no entry condition, so a subtask can succeed in a form its successor cannot use. We present BATON. Against (1), BATON makes the subtask the unit of exploration: each is explored in the cheap short-horizon regime and its solution stored in memory; a long-horizon trajectory is then composed from these solutions rather than discovered whole. Cost becomes additive (T*K) and every failure is attributed to a single stage. Against (2), BATON equips exploration with a transition-aware memory. Within a subtask, a verifier agent governs the invocation transition: the VLA is called only after the wrist view confirms the scene is ready. Across subtasks, a handoff transition restores an entry state disturbed by the predecessor's residue, and a lookahead transition selects the strategy whose outcome the successor can inherit. No parameters are updated. On the long-horizon benchmark RoboMemArena, BATON improves task success by 11.6% and cumulative success by 14.9% over the SoTA.
2608.16889.paper_summary_zh: 長期機器人操作將許多接觸豐富的技能鏈接成一個多階段任務。視覺-語言-行動（VLA）模型越來越能掌握個別技能，但這個鏈接仍然失敗：錯誤的累積超出了策略的修正能力，且一個子任務靜默地限制了下一個子任務。一個有前景的方案是凍結VLA並讓一個LLM代理負責：它用語言進行計劃，在自由空間中使用解析原語移動，僅在接觸豐富的片段中調用VLA，並將適應性寫入語言記憶。應用於長期任務時，它會出現兩次失敗。（1）能力來自於測試時的整體任務探索，其成本在階段上是乘法的：如果一個階段需要T次實驗，則一個K階段的任務約需要T^K，而一次失敗並不揭示是哪個階段造成的。（2）它沒有轉換的表示：VLA原語攜帶一個退出條件但沒有進入條件，因此一個子任務可以以其後繼無法使用的形式成功。我們提出BATON。針對（1），BATON使子任務成為探索的單位：每個子任務在便宜的短期範疇內進行探索，其解決方案存儲在記憶中；然後，長期軌跡是從這些解決方案組成，而不是整體發現。成本變為加法（T*K），每次失敗都歸因於單一階段。針對（2），BATON為探索配備了轉換感知記憶。在一個子任務內，驗證代理管理調用轉換：僅在手腕視圖確認場景準備好後才調用VLA。在子任務之間，交接轉換恢復被前任殘留物擾亂的進入狀態，而前瞻轉換選擇其結果可以被後繼繼承的策略。沒有參數被更新。在長期基準RoboMemArena上，BATON將任務成功率提高了11.6％，累積成功率提高了14.9％，超過了目前的最佳技術。
